acetabulum.definition: The hip socket, where the thighbone meets the hips. In dinosaurs it is open in the middle. Supraacetabular means "above the hip socket".

acromion.definition: A projection near the top of the shoulder blade, where shoulder muscles attach.

alveolus.definition: A tooth socket in the jaw. Alveolar means "of the tooth sockets".

amphicoelous.definition: Describes a vertebra whose main body is hollow at both the front and the back.
amphicoelous.etymology: Greek amphi, "on both sides", and koilos, "hollow".

anterior.definition: Toward the front of the animal, the end with the head. The opposite of posterior.

antorbital-fenestra.definition: An opening in the side of the skull between the nostril and the eye socket. The antorbital fossa is the hollow around it.
antorbital-fenestra.etymology: Latin ante, "before", orbita, the eye socket, and fenestra, "window".

appendicular.definition: Of the limbs and of the shoulder and hip bones they attach to, as opposed to the skull and backbone.

articulated.definition: Of bones: found still joined together as they were in life. Disarticulated bones were found separated from each other.

articulation.definition: A joint between bones. Articular means "forming a joint".

associated-skeleton.definition: Bones found together and thought to come from a single animal, though not joined as they were in life.

astragalus.definition: An ankle bone at the bottom of the shinbone. In many dinosaurs it sends a tall plate, the ascending process, up the front of the shin.

atlas.definition: The first vertebra of the neck, on which the skull rests and turns.
atlas.etymology: Atlas of Greek myth, who held up the heavens.

autapomorphy.definition: A feature found in only one species or genus, which sets it apart from all its relatives. Autapomorphies show that a name represents a distinct animal.
autapomorphy.etymology: Greek autos, "self", apo, "away from", and morphe, "form".

axial-skeleton.definition: The skull, backbone and ribs, as opposed to the limbs and the bones they attach to.

basin.definition: A low-lying region where sediment built up over a long time, forming the layers of rock that fossils are found in.

basisphenoid.definition: A bone of the floor of the braincase. Its basipterygoid processes reach down and forward to meet the palate.

bonebed.definition: A layer of rock packed with the bones of many animals, often buried together.

boss.definition: A rounded, thickened bump of bone, such as the bosses on the snouts of some horned dinosaurs.

braincase.definition: The box of bone around the brain, at the back of the skull.

calcaneum.definition: An ankle bone at the bottom of the fibula, beside the astragalus.

carina.definition: The sharp cutting edge along the front or back of a tooth, often lined with denticles.

carpal.definition: One of the small bones of the wrist. The carpus is the wrist.

caudal-vertebra.definition: A vertebra of the tail. Caudal means "of the tail" or "toward the tail".

centrum.definition: The spool-shaped main body of a vertebra, which bears the weight. The spinal cord runs along its top, inside the neural arch.

cervical-vertebra.definition: A vertebra of the neck. Cervical means "of the neck".

character.definition: In a phylogenetic analysis, a feature that differs among the animals studied, such as the shape of a bone, recorded for each animal to work out how they are related.

chevron.definition: A small bone that hangs below the joint between two tail vertebrae, protecting blood vessels and anchoring tail muscles.
chevron.etymology: French, a V-shaped stripe, after its shape.

chimera.definition: A specimen, or a name based on one, made up of bones that turned out to come from more than one kind of animal.
chimera.etymology: The Chimera of Greek myth, a monster made of parts of several animals.

clade.definition: A group made up of an ancestor and all of its descendants. Every branch of a family tree is a clade.

cnemial-crest.definition: A ridge at the front of the top of the shinbone, where the muscles that straighten the knee attach.

combined-directions.definition: Words that join two directions. Anteroposterior means "from front to back", so a bone that is anteroposteriorly long is long from front to back; anterodorsal means "toward the front and the top".

condyle.definition: A rounded knob at the end of a bone that forms part of a joint.

consensus-tree.definition: A family tree that combines several equally good trees from one analysis, keeping only the groupings they all agree on.

convergence.definition: The evolution of similar features in animals that aren't closely related, often because they lived in similar ways.

coracoid.definition: A plate of bone at the lower end of the shoulder blade, forming part of the shoulder joint.
coracoid.etymology: Greek korax, "crow", after its beak-like shape in mammals.

coronoid.definition: A raised part of the lower jaw, behind the teeth, where jaw-closing muscles attach. In some dinosaurs it is a separate small bone.
coronoid.etymology: Greek korone, "crow", after its beak-like shape.

cranium.definition: The skull, or the part of it that encloses the brain. Cranial means "of the skull"; cranially means "toward the head".

crest.definition: A ridge or blade of bone, such as the hollow crests on the heads of some hadrosaurs.

cursorial.definition: Built for running, with long, slender legs.

deltopectoral-crest.definition: A ridge on the upper arm bone where the shoulder and chest muscles attach.

dental-battery.definition: Rows of tightly packed teeth that worked together as one grinding or slicing surface, with new teeth constantly growing in to replace worn ones, as in hadrosaurs and ceratopsids.

dentary.definition: The main bone of the lower jaw, which carries the lower teeth.

denticle.definition: One of the small bumps along the cutting edge of a tooth, like the teeth of a saw. Serrated teeth have them.

deposit.definition: Sediment laid down by water, wind or other means, which can harden into rock.

derived.definition: Describes a member of a group that branched off later in the group's family tree, or a feature that changed from the ancestral condition. The opposite of early-diverging.

diagnosis.definition: The list of features that sets a species or genus apart from its relatives, published with its name or in a later study. A diagnostic feature is one that identifies it.

diapophysis.definition: A projection on the side of a vertebra where the upper head of a rib attaches.

diastema.definition: A gap in the tooth row, such as the one between the beak and the cheek teeth of many plant-eating dinosaurs.

distal.definition: Farther from the body, or from where a limb or bone attaches. The knee end of the thighbone is its distal end. On a tooth, distal means "toward the back of the jaw".

dorsal.definition: Toward the back or top of the animal, the side the backbone runs along. The opposite of ventral. Dorsal also names the vertebrae of the back.

dorsal-vertebra.definition: A vertebra of the back, between the neck and the hips. Most carry ribs.

early-diverging.definition: Describes a member of a group that branched off early in the group's family tree, near its base. It need not be older or simpler than its relatives. Also called basal.

epiparietal.definition: One of the bony points along the edge of a horned dinosaur's frill.

epipophysis.definition: A bony projection above the postzygapophysis of a neck vertebra, where neck muscles attached.

epoch.definition: A division of geologic time within a period, such as the Late Cretaceous within the Cretaceous.

facet.definition: A small, flat surface where one bone meets another.

family.definition: A rank in traditional classification that groups related genera. Family names end in -idae, as in Tyrannosauridae.

femur.definition: The thighbone. Femoral means "of the femur".

fenestra.definition: A large opening in a bone or between bones, especially in the skull.

fibula.definition: The thin bone beside the shinbone in the lower leg.

flange.definition: A thin rim or plate of bone that sticks out.

foramen.definition: A hole through a bone, for a nerve or blood vessel to pass through.

formation.definition: A body of rock that geologists map and name as a unit, such as the Hell Creek Formation. Fossils are dated and compared by the formations they come from.

fossa.definition: A shallow hollow in a bone.

fragmentary.definition: Of a fossil: known only from broken or incomplete pieces.

frill.definition: The bony shield that extends back over the neck from the skull of a horned dinosaur.

frontal.definition: One of the paired bones of the skull roof above the eyes.

furcula.definition: The wishbone: the fused collarbones of theropod dinosaurs, including birds.

fused.definition: Of bones: grown together into one. Bones often fuse as an animal matures, so unfused bones can mark a young animal.

gastralia.definition: Belly ribs: thin bones in the wall of the belly that are not attached to the backbone.

girdle.definition: The bones a pair of limbs attach to: the shoulder bones for the forelimbs and the hip bones for the hindlimbs.

glenoid.definition: The socket of the shoulder joint, where the upper arm bone meets the shoulder bones.

gondwana.definition: The southern supercontinent made up of today's South America, Africa, Madagascar, India, Antarctica and Australia, which broke apart during the age of dinosaurs.
gondwana.etymology: From a region of India, "forest of the Gonds".

grade.definition: A set of animals at a similar stage of evolution that don't form a single clade, such as the early sauropodomorphs once grouped together as prosauropods.

holotype.definition: The single specimen a species' name is tied to, chosen when the species is named. Other fossils are compared with it to decide whether they belong to the same species.

horncore.definition: The bony core of a horn, which in life was covered by a sheath of horn.

humerus.definition: The upper arm bone. Humeral means "of the humerus".

hypertrophied.definition: Enlarged far beyond the usual size.

hyposphene.definition: An extra joint between back vertebrae: a wedge below the joint surfaces at the back of one vertebra, the hyposphene, fits into a notch, the hypantrum, in the next.

ilium.definition: The upper hip bone, joined to the backbone.

incertae-sedis.definition: Used for an animal that belongs to a larger group when where it fits within that group can't be decided.

intercentrum.definition: A small wedge of bone below and between the main bodies of neighboring vertebrae. In dinosaurs it is found mainly at the front of the neck, as part of the atlas.

ischium.definition: The hip bone that points down and back.

isolated.definition: Of a fossil: found on its own, apart from any skeleton, as with an isolated tooth. An isolated bone is hard to assign to a species.

jugal.definition: The cheekbone, below the eye socket.

juvenile.definition: A young animal, not yet fully grown. A subadult was nearly grown.

labial.definition: On the side of a tooth or jaw that faces the lips or cheek, outside the mouth. The opposite of lingual.

lacrimal.definition: A bone in front of the eye socket, between the eye and the antorbital fenestra.

lamina.definition: A thin plate or ridge of bone. On many dinosaur vertebrae, laminae brace the vertebra like struts, each named for the parts it joins.

lateral.definition: Toward the side of the animal, away from the line that runs down the middle of its body. The opposite of medial.

laurasia.definition: The northern supercontinent made up of today's North America, Europe and most of Asia, which broke apart during the age of dinosaurs.

least-inclusive-clade.definition: The smallest clade that contains all the named animals. Defining a clade this way picks out the last common ancestor of those animals and all its descendants.

lectotype.definition: A specimen chosen after a species was named, from among its syntypes, to be the single specimen its name is tied to.

lineage.definition: A line of descent: an ancestor and the descendants that follow from it over time.

lingual.definition: On the side of a tooth or jaw that faces the tongue, inside the mouth. The opposite of labial.

locality.definition: The place where a fossil was found. The type locality is where the holotype was found.

mandible.definition: The lower jaw, made of several bones on each side.

manus.definition: The hand. Manual means "of the hand".

maxilla.definition: The main tooth-bearing bone of the upper jaw, behind the premaxilla. Maxillary means "of the maxilla".

medial.definition: Toward the line that runs down the middle of the animal's body. The opposite of lateral.

mesial.definition: On a tooth, the side toward the front of the jaw, following the curve of the tooth row. The opposite of distal.

metacarpal.definition: One of the bones of the palm of the hand, between the wrist and the fingers.

metatarsal.definition: One of the long bones of the foot, between the ankle and the toes. Many dinosaurs walked with them raised off the ground.
metatarsal.etymology: Greek meta, "after", and tarsos, "flat of the foot".

monophyletic.definition: Describes a group that includes an ancestor and all of its descendants. A monophyletic group is a clade.

monotypic.definition: Containing only one member: a monotypic genus has a single species.

naris.definition: A nostril, or the opening in the skull for it.

nasal.definition: The bone on top of the snout, above the nostrils. Nasal also means "of the nose".

neotype.definition: A specimen chosen to replace a holotype that has been lost or destroyed, or that can no longer be identified, so the name has a specimen to rest on again.

neural-arch.definition: The arch of bone on top of a vertebra's main body, which encloses the spinal cord. The neural spine and most of the vertebra's other projections grow from it.

neural-spine.definition: The blade or rod of bone that sticks up from the top of a vertebra, where back muscles and ligaments attach. Very tall neural spines formed sails or humps in some dinosaurs.

neurovascular.definition: For nerves and blood vessels, such as the small neurovascular openings along the jaws.

node-based.definition: Describes a clade defined as the last common ancestor of two or more named animals and all of its descendants.

nomen-dubium.definition: A name based on fossils that can't be reliably told apart from those of related animals, so it may not represent a distinct species or genus.

nomen-nudum.definition: A name published without the description or other details the naming rules require, so it isn't a valid name.

non-avian-dinosaur.definition: Any dinosaur other than a bird. Birds are dinosaurs, so "non-avian" sets apart the rest.

obturator.definition: Names features of the lower hip bones near the obturator nerve: the opening or notch in the pubis that the nerve passed through, and the obturator process of the ischium.

occiput.definition: The back of the skull, around the opening for the spinal cord. The occipital condyle is the knob where the skull meets the neck; the paroccipital processes stick out to the sides.

olecranon.definition: The point of the elbow, at the top of the ulna.

ontogeny.definition: The growth and development of an animal from hatching to adulthood. Ontogenetic changes can make young and old animals of one species look like different species.

opisthocoelous.definition: Describes a vertebra whose main body is rounded at the front and hollow at the back, so each one fits into the next like a ball and socket.

orbit.definition: The eye socket. Supraorbital means "above the eye socket"; preorbital, "in front of it".

ossified-tendons.definition: Tendons that turned to bone. In many ornithischian dinosaurs they formed a lattice of rods along the back and tail that stiffened them.

osteoderm.definition: A bony plate or knob set in the skin, such as those that made up the armor of ankylosaurs. Dermal means "of the skin".

palate.definition: The roof of the mouth. In dinosaurs it is made of several paired bones, among them the palatines, pterygoids and ectopterygoids.

pangaea.definition: The supercontinent that joined nearly all of Earth's land when the first dinosaurs lived, before it split into Laurasia and Gondwana.

paraphyletic.definition: Describes a group that includes an ancestor but only some of its descendants, such as reptiles without birds.

parapophysis.definition: A projection or facet on the side of a vertebra where the lower head of a rib attaches.

paratype.definition: A specimen the authors who named a species listed alongside the holotype. Paratypes help show what the species was like, but the name isn't tied to them.

parietal.definition: One of the bones of the skull roof behind the eyes, over the brain. In horned dinosaurs the parietals form most of the frill.

pectoral-girdle.definition: The shoulder bones the forelimbs attach to: the shoulder blade and coracoid on each side.

peduncle.definition: A short stalk of bone. On the ilium, the pubic and ischial peduncles join it to the other hip bones.

pelvis.definition: The hip bones: the ilium, ischium and pubis on each side, joined to the sacrum.

pennaceous.definition: Of feathers: having a central shaft with a flat vane on each side, like a bird's flight feathers, rather than being simple filaments.

pes.definition: The foot. Pedal means "of the foot".

phalanx.definition: One of the bones of a finger or toe.

phylogenetic-analysis.definition: A study that works out how animals are related by comparing many of their features, usually with software that finds the family trees that best fit those features.

platycoelous.definition: Describes a vertebra whose main body is flat at both ends.

plesiomorphic.definition: Describes an ancestral feature, inherited from a distant ancestor and shared widely, so it says little about which animals are most closely related.

pleurocoel.definition: A hollow or opening in the side of a vertebra's main body, made by an air sac.

pneumatic.definition: Hollowed by air sacs that grew into the bone from the lungs, as in birds. Pneumatic bones were lighter for their size.

pollex.definition: The first finger of the hand, equivalent to the human thumb. In many sauropodomorphs it carried a large claw.

polytomy.definition: A point on a family tree where three or more branches split at once, because the analysis couldn't settle the order in which they branched.

postcranial.definition: Of the skeleton behind the skull: everything but the head.

posterior.definition: Toward the back of the animal, the end with the tail. The opposite of anterior.

postorbital.definition: The bone behind the eye socket. In horned dinosaurs it carries the horn above the eye.
postorbital.etymology: Latin post, "behind", and orbita, the eye socket.

preacetabular-process.definition: The part of the ilium that extends forward of the hip socket. The postacetabular process extends behind it.

predentary.definition: A toothless bone at the front of the lower jaw of ornithischian dinosaurs, which carried a horny beak.

prefrontal.definition: A small bone above and in front of the eye socket.

premaxilla.definition: The bone at the front tip of the upper jaw. In many dinosaurs it carries teeth; in others, a beak.

preoccupied.definition: Of a name: already given to another animal, so it can't be used again. The later animal needs a replacement name.

prepubic-process.definition: In ornithischian dinosaurs, a blade of the pubis that points forward.

presacral.definition: Of the vertebrae in front of the hips: those of the neck and back.

process.definition: A projection of bone, often where a muscle or ligament attaches.

procoelous.definition: Describes a vertebra whose main body is hollow at the front and rounded at the back, the reverse of opisthocoelous.

proximal.definition: Closer to the body, or to where a limb or bone attaches. The hip end of the thighbone is its proximal end. The opposite of distal.

pubis.definition: The hip bone that points down and forward in saurischian dinosaurs, and down and back in ornithischians and birds.

quadrate.definition: The bone at the back of the skull that forms the upper half of the jaw joint.

quadratojugal.definition: A bone at the lower back corner of the skull that joins the quadrate to the jugal.

radiation.definition: A burst of evolution in which one lineage splits into many species that spread into different ways of life.

radius.definition: One of the two bones of the forearm, beside the ulna.

ramus.definition: A branch of a bone, such as a bar of the upper jaw or each half of the lower jaw.

referred-specimen.definition: A fossil assigned to a species after it was named, because it shares the species' features. The name isn't tied to it, and a later study can move it to another species.

retroarticular-process.definition: A projection of the lower jaw behind the jaw joint, where the muscle that opens the jaw attaches.

rostral.definition: Toward the tip of the snout.

rostral-bone.definition: A toothless bone at the front of the upper jaw of horned dinosaurs, which carried the upper beak.

rugose.definition: Rough and wrinkled, often where a muscle attached or a horny covering grew.

sacral-vertebra.definition: One of the vertebrae joined to the hip bones. Fused together, they form the sacrum.

sagittal.definition: Running from front to back along the middle of the body, in the plane that divides the left side from the right.

scapula.definition: The shoulder blade. Fused to the coracoid, it forms a scapulocoracoid.

shaft.definition: The long middle part of a limb bone, between its two ends.

sister-taxon.definition: The closest relative of a group on a family tree: the two share an ancestor that no other group shares.

skin-impression.definition: A mark left in the rock by an animal's skin, showing its scales or other covering.

specific-epithet.definition: The second part of a species' name, such as rex in Tyrannosaurus rex. It names the species only together with its genus.

splenial.definition: A thin bone on the inner side of the lower jaw.

squamosal.definition: A bone at the back corner of the skull, above the jaw joint. In horned dinosaurs it forms the sides of the frill.

stage.definition: A division of geologic time within an epoch, lasting a few million years, such as the Maastrichtian.

stem.definition: The extinct relatives of a group that branched off before its last common ancestor. A stem-based clade is defined as everything closer to one animal than to another.

sternum.definition: The breastbone. In many dinosaurs it was a pair of flat sternal plates.

strata.definition: Layers of rock. Beds are the thinnest named layers.

subfamily.definition: A group of related genera within a family. Subfamily names end in -inae, as in Tyrannosaurinae.

superfamily.definition: A group of related families. Superfamily names end in -oidea, as in Tyrannosauroidea.

surangular.definition: A bone at the back and top of the lower jaw, in front of the jaw joint.

suture.definition: The seam where two bones meet and grow together.

symphysis.definition: A joint where bones from the left and right sides meet in the middle, such as where the two halves of the lower jaw join at the chin.

synapomorphy.definition: A new feature shared by the members of a group, inherited from their common ancestor, that sets the group apart from others. Synapomorphies are the evidence for a clade.
synapomorphy.etymology: Greek syn, "together", apo, "away from", and morphe, "form".

synonym.definition: One of two or more names given to the same animal. The oldest name usually takes priority as the senior synonym; later names become junior synonyms and fall out of use.

syntype.definition: One of several specimens that together served as the basis for a name, when no single holotype was chosen.

tarsal.definition: One of the small bones of the ankle. The tarsus is the ankle.

taxon.definition: Any named group of living things, such as a species, a genus or a clade.

temporal-fenestra.definition: One of the openings in the skull behind the eye socket, through which jaw muscles passed: one on the skull roof (supratemporal) and one on each side (infratemporal or laterotemporal).

tibia.definition: The shinbone, the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

tibiotarsus.definition: In birds and some of their closest relatives, the shinbone fused with the upper ankle bones.

tooth-crown.definition: The part of a tooth that sticks out above the gum, covered in enamel.

transverse.definition: Running across the body from side to side.

transverse-process.definition: A projection that sticks out sideways from a vertebra, where ribs or muscles attach.

trochanter.definition: A bump or ridge on the thighbone where hip and leg muscles attach. Dinosaurs have several, such as the lesser and fourth trochanters.

tubercle.definition: A small bump on a bone, often where a muscle or ligament attaches. A tuberosity is a larger one.

type-species.definition: The species a genus name is tied to. A genus is defined by its type species, as a species is defined by its holotype.

type-specimen.definition: A specimen a species' name is formally tied to: the holotype, or a lectotype or neotype chosen later.

ulna.definition: One of the two bones of the forearm. The point of the elbow is at its upper end.

ungual.definition: The last bone of a finger or toe, which carried the claw or hoof.

valid.definition: Of a name: properly published and the accepted name for its animal, not a synonym or a doubtful name.

ventral.definition: Toward the belly or underside of the animal. The opposite of dorsal.

vertebra.definition: One of the bones of the backbone, which runs from the skull to the tip of the tail.

wildcard-taxon.definition: An animal whose position jumps around a family tree from one analysis to the next, usually because too little of it is known.

zygapophysis.definition: One of the paired projections that link one vertebra to the next. The prezygapophyses at the front of a vertebra fit against the postzygapophyses at the back of the one ahead.
